description.value: The study compared hemodynamic brain responses and task-related functional connectivity between big wave surfers and non-big wave surfers while they viewed positive and negative affective images varying in arousal.

design.value: A convenience sample of 25 surfers was categorized into big wave surfers (BWS, n=15) and non-big wave surfers (CON, n=10). After one participant was withdrawn for claustrophobia and one excluded for falling asleep, 23 participants were included in the analyses. Participants viewed 160 IAPS images in an event-related fMRI design, with 20 fixation trials.

description.value: Measured participants’ subjective emotional responses to the IAPS images.
Measured self-reported levels of sensation seeking across intensity of an experience and novelty of an experience scales.
Assessed participants’ positive and negative feelings experienced over the past week.
Assessed self-reported levels of fear toward various circumstances, objects, or other stimuli.
Those who regularly surfed waves >20 feet in height using the Hawaiian measurement system.

inclusion_criteria.value: Regularly surfed waves >20 feet in height using the Hawaiian measurement system.

clinical_characteristics.value: Surfing experience: 26 ± 8 years; current surfing activity: 13 ± 10 hours/week; professional or semi-professional: 12.

description.value: Those who had not surfed waves of >20 feet in height using the Hawaiian measurement system.

inclusion_criteria.value: Had not surfed waves of this height.

clinical_characteristics.value: Surfing experience: 21 ± 10 years; current surfing activity: 6 ± 3 hours/week; professional or semi-professional: 1.

task_description.value: Participants viewed a series of images from the International Affective Picture System while undergoing brain fMRI. Images were categorized by valence and arousal into high arousal positive, high arousal negative, low arousal positive, and low arousal negative groups.

design_type.value: event-related design with jittered inter-stimulus interval

instructions.value: Participants were asked to view all images presented on the screen. No tasks related to regulation were instructed.

stimuli.value: 160 IAPS photographs, with 40 images selected from each of the high arousal positive, high arousal negative, low arousal positive, and low arousal negative groups; photographs were edited to reduce saturation by 30%.

task_performance_measures.value: After the fMRI, participants were asked whether they were able to remain attentive to all images.

instrument.value: 3 T MRI scanner (Achieva, Philips, Best, Netherlands)

description.value: Functional BOLD signals were acquired with a multi-shot gradient echo echoplanar imaging sequence. Twenty-two axial slices covering the whole brain were acquired.

description.value: Anatomical images of the functional slice locations were obtained with gradient echo sequences in the sagittal plane.

Images were realigned and corrected for slice timing; a mean functional image was constructed, co-registered with the high-resolution structural image, segmented for normalization with affine registration followed by nonlinear transformation, normalized, and smoothed with an 8-mm Gaussian kernel at full width at half maximum.

application of normalization parameters to corresponding functional image volumes
smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of 8 mm at full width at half maximum

hrf_model.value: canonical hemodynamic response function and its temporal derivative

model_settings.value: Image onset in each trial was convolved with the canonical hemodynamic response function and its temporal derivative. Realignment parameters in all six dimensions were entered in the model. Data were high-pass filtered with a 1/128 Hz cutoff, and serial autocorrelation was corrected by a first-degree autoregressive or AR(1) model.

estimator.value: random-effect group analysis for resulting contrast images

model_settings.value: The model examined the main effects of group, arousal, and valence as well as the interaction effect.

The hemodynamic responses of HAP, HAN, LAP, LAN, and FIX formed the psychological regressors. Physiological neural-signal time series were multiplied by onset times of the five conditions separately and re-convolved with the canonical hemodynamic response function. Psychological regressors, the physiological variable, and PPI variables were entered in a whole-brain GLM.

level.value: first-level analysis followed by random-effect group analysis
